h: Making Ourselves Through Torah and Inheriting Its Light

p: which I teach you to do,
וּבָאתֶם וִירִשְׁתֶּם אֶת הָאָרֶץ וְגוֹ׳ (דְּבָרִים ד, א)
and come and inherit the land," etc. (Devarim 4:1).
in order to inherit Eretz Yisrael,
they would be exempt from the 613 mitzvos?
The term "to do" is also difficult:
so why is it precise with the word "to do"?
as Hashem my God commanded me,
to do so in the midst of the land
which you are coming to inherit."
And there too it is difficult:
do the mitzvos depend specifically on the land?
apply outside the land as well!
And afterward it is further written (there, 14):
"And Hashem commanded me at that time
to teach you statutes and laws,
for you to do them in the land," etc.;
it also made the mitzvos dependent
it should have said "to do them."
are by passive refraining as well,
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמַר (סַנְהֶדְרִין צט, ב)
"as though he made the words of Torah, etc.;
as though he made himself, etc.;
"as though he made the words of Torah"
the power of the words of Torah
through his longing for the Torah.
הַיְינוּ עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (מִשְׁלֵי כ, כז)
that is, according to what it says (Mishlei 20:27):
"The lamp of Hashem is the soul of man";
that he draws down the root of his soul
so that Hashem Yisbarach causes to shine
the lamp of Hashem in his heart.
of "we will do and we will hear":
"we will do" — the words of Torah,
that is, that there shine in the heart
"the lamp of Hashem, the soul of man."
And this is what it says:
means that the words of Torah
are fixed and engraved in the heart;
are the essential bodies of Torah.
does not refer to the performance of the mitzvos,
to make the words of Torah,
only through the holiness of the land.
And this is "so that you may live":
that is, that it be from the root of life,
from the side of the Tree of Life.
"And come and inherit the land," etc.:
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רמג, ב)
we call it Torah she'b'al peh"
הוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכט, ב)
"like an inheritance that has no interruption";
the light of Torah she'b'al peh
that will be only from the side of good,
the aspect of the Written Torah.
And this is what it says afterward:
"to do so in the midst of the land"
meaning that when you enter the land
you will merit to make the words of Torah,
"And Hashem commanded me at that time"
of the conquest of Sichon and Og,
when they conquered the root of the kelipah
and they were then at a high level,
when the Written Torah was fixed in them,
for the light of Torah she'b'al peh;
the aspect of the Written Torah
intends as in the words of Rava above:
to draw down from the root
"the lamp of Hashem, the soul of man."
And therefore it is written with a kaf,
(as is written in the holy Zohar in many places),
for it is a drawing down from the root,
"as though he made the words of Torah,"
like the meaning of "we will do"
that is, to draw down the words of Torah,
And this they will merit only in the land:
the holiness of the land will help
to merit the light of Torah she'b'al peh

p: אֵת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה ה׳ בְּבַעַל פְּעוֹר
what Hashem did with Baal Peor"
And before this it is written (there 3:29):
which has no connection or place here,
and this was also already written
for it is known that the root of the serpent's corruption
was to bring desire into eating;
and through this there came about
for of the man it is written,
"that it was absorbed in the 248 limbs";
there was no waste from eating
when Adam HaRishon was in Gan Eden,
who brought in the power of desire
did the excess and waste come about.
of the worship of one who exposes himself to Peor
even if he intends to degrade it,
he thereby gives power to the kelipah
which are from the root of the serpent.
and this is what it says:
"to atone for the deed of Peor."
And this is what it says:
"And we dwelt in the valley opposite Beis Peor"
when the days of mourning for Moshe were completed,
"And we dwelt in the valley opposite Beis Peor"
to rectify the root of the serpent's corruption.
in the manner that it is expounded
that he sought to dwell in tranquility.
And about this it says afterward,
in the manner of what it says
that from now the matter has changed for the good.
that is, that they were called so
"for you have striven with God," etc.;
and to rectify the serpent's corruption.
that the words of Torah be engraved in the heart.
And this is the meaning of what it says:
אֵת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה ה׳ בְּבַעַל פְּעוֹר וְגוֹ׳
what Hashem did with Baal Peor," etc.
that is, that they merited the power of seeing,
all the vitality from the kelipah
"And you who cleave to Hashem your God"
Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
from the passage of this wicked one:
and he cast impurity into her
for you are attached at the root;
which is from the side of the Tree of Life,
mixture of good and evil at all,
which came about through the kelipah of the serpent.
denotes the day of the giving of the Torah;
and at the Stand at Har Sinai
for they would not have died
that is, they merited to rectify
all the corruption of the serpent.
And this is what it says afterward:
one brings in the light "that it is good."
And it says "see" in the singular
and "I have taught you" in the plural;
for the teaching is for all Yisrael,
and the root of his soul.
And this is the meaning of
"Moshe rejoiced in the gift of his portion":
to bring in through his seeing
like the seeing of Hashem Yisbarach
from the light "that it is good."
And at the second meal we say:
the light "that it is good" permanently;
in Pri Etz Chaim, Sha'ar HaShabbos,
